correctness.rationale: For any invertible two-row restriction T, the identity kappa(T)^2=||T||_F^2/sigma_min(T)^2-1 holds exactly in dimension two. E-optimality orders the minima, while the global row-leverage ratio bounds the Frobenius trace ratio by rho. These imply the displayed dimension-free inequality and kappa ratio at most sqrt(2rho-1). At rho=1, equal two-row Frobenius traces make both optimizations equivalent, including ties. The example has orthonormal columns, row leverages n,4,1 divided by n+1, exactly classified full-rank pairs, and a symmetric invertible Krylov realization. Exact symbolic calculations checked 231 family/Krylov identities, while 1320 random frames corroborated the bound; no finite experiment replaces the all-dimension algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: An accessible earlier mathematical record already establishes the order sqrt(n) worst-case gap between globally E-optimal and best-conditioned two-row restrictions; that distinction and its Krylov realization are acknowledged as prior work and not claimed here. Its N-dependent theorem does not imply the new leverage-dependent bound, which is uniformly O(1) for bounded leverage ratio even as N grows, nor its exact coincidence at uniform leverage. Bergermann motivates sigma_min as a useful Krylov sketch proxy without the present dimension-free conditional comparison. The related sensor-design reference remains an explicitly disclosed bibliographic risk; the present narrow numerical-linear-algebra theorem is assessed as original under the inspected sources, not as conclusively unique.

The illustrative sqrt(rho) gap is mathematically close to a previously published sqrt(n) gap and is not asserted as a distinct novelty.

value.rationale: The motivating numerical choice maximizes the least singular value of a coordinate restriction while subspace distortion is a condition number. Prior work proves that their worst-case gap grows with ambient size; this theorem resolves the motivated near-incoherent case instead: bounded leverage imbalance gives a dimension-free constant approximation to optimal distortion, equal leverage gives exact optimization equivalence, and rho=1+delta yields relative distortion at most sqrt(1+2delta). This is a structural design guarantee with direct relevance to row-balanced Krylov bases, rather than a recomputation of the known sqrt(N) worst-case example. It does not claim a result for actual solver convergence or that the constant is sharp.
